🇮🇶🇮🇷 Iraqi troops have entered a militia stronghold the government couldn’t touch for over a decade.

The zone just outside Baghdad has been run for years by Kataib Hezbollah, Iraq’s most powerful Iran-backed militia.

Things came to a head when a government inquiry tied the group to oil smuggling in the area.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi then gave it until today to leave the area.

Iran’s Quds Force chief Esmail Qaani reportedly traveled to Baghdad to help settle the standoff.

A deal came together before the deadline, and the troops moved in.

What nobody knows yet is whether the militia is actually leaving.

Source: The New York Times / Writers: Daniyal, Marie
